dispute.riderClaim: I was charged a no-show fee but I was only a few minutes late. The driver cancelled on me.
dispute.driverStatement: I arrived at the pickup, messaged and called the rider, and waited more than five minutes before cancelling.

cases.summary: The driver met every condition required to retain the no-show fee under NS-1. GPS data shows the driver came within 31 m of the pickup (limit 150 m) and waited 430 seconds from first entering the threshold until cancelling (minimum 300 s). The driver also made three recorded contact attempts before cancelling (CHAT-01, CHAT-03, CALL-01), exceeding the minimum of one. The rider's own message acknowledged the driver's arrival and promised to arrive in 2 minutes but did not appear within the wait window. The charge is valid and the driver should keep the fee.

arguments.claim: The driver came within 150 metres of the pickup point, satisfying the first NS-1 condition.
The driver waited at least 300 seconds from first coming within 150 metres until cancelling (430 s), satisfying the second NS-1 condition.
The driver made at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling; three attempts were logged (arrival message, follow-up message, and a call), satisfying the third NS-1 condition.
The rider acknowledged the driver's arrival and said they were coming in 2 minutes, but the driver still waited well beyond that before cancelling, so the no-show was the rider's failure to appear.
The no-show fee of S$5.00 was correctly charged and paid, with valid arithmetic and no anomalies.

counterevidence.claim: The driver's follow-up message contained a threat ('I will report you and call the police'), which is negative conduct and may weigh against the driver's professionalism, though it does not negate the NS-1 conditions.
The rider claims they were only a few minutes late, which is consistent with their 'coming in 2 minutes' message; however, the driver's wait exceeded the policy minimum regardless.

cases.summary: The rider was charged a S$5.00 no-show fee after the driver cancelled. The rider claims they were only a few minutes late. However, the GPS evidence shows the driver met all three NS-1 conditions: closest approach 31 m (within 150 m), waited 430 s (over the 300 s minimum), and made 3 contact attempts before cancelling. Under NS-1, the no-show fee is properly retained, and NS-2's refund trigger (any condition unmet) does not apply.
